speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the specific nature of your gait and limb ataxia, such as whether it is cerebellar, sensory, or ataxic, and when these symptoms first began. Additionally, could you detail your significant medical history, including any past infections, autoimmune conditions, or recent vaccinations?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunken" appearance suggests cerebellar involvement. Has this ataxia progressed steadily over time, or has it fluctuated? Also, do you experience any double vision, slurred speech, or numbness in your limbs alongside these motor symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease and use of natalizumab, combined with new-onset cerebellar ataxia, this is highly suspicious for JC virus reactivation. I am requesting an MRI of the brain without contrast to visualize characteristic white matter lesions.
